body:
Loading text through the recovering parser (`MarkerParse.of_text` → `Parser.to_zipper`) is about 2.5× faster, with the same parse. This is part of [#2609, "Performance Challenges (Fall 2026)"](https://github.com/hazelgrove/hazel/issues/2609): that parser is what makes the round-trip and doc-slide test groups slow.

## Why it was slow

`to_zipper` ran the full typing path (`Insert.go`) once per character, and every insertion re-grouted the whole run of siblings it landed in. On one long expression that is quadratic. A profile put about a third of the time in `regrout_affix` and another third in garbage collection, most of it from rebuilding those lists.

## What changed

Four commits, each checked on its own:

1. **`Siblings.rescan` returns its argument when nothing needs rescanning**, so `rescan_reassemble` can see "no change" by identity instead of structurally comparing every sibling.
2. **Text loads a token at a time.** With `~by_run`, when the caret is between tokens, the longest run that stays one operand (or one operator) goes in as a single insertion. That run is exactly what typing would keep appending to anyway. Brackets, quotes, comment delimiters and whitespace still go in one character at a time.
3. **`rescan` also reports "no change" while a tile is incomplete.** Mid-parse there is almost always an open tile (a `let` waiting for its `in`), so (1) rarely fired. `Segment.rescan_changed` now says whether any piece came out different.
4. **Re-grout once at the end instead of after every insertion.** `Insert.go` and its helpers (and `Zipper.put_down_target`) take `~regrout=true`. Only `to_zipper ~by_run` passes `false`, and it re-grouts once when the text is in.

Only `MarkerParse.of_text` passes `~by_run`. Typing, paste and deletion keep the defaults, so they behave exactly as before.

## Checking the parse is the same

- **All 72 `hazel-programs`:** identical printed text and identical structure against `dev`, comparing every tile's label, mold and shards, every grout shape and every whitespace piece (ids aside).
- **Coverage of (4):** while developing it, a temporary counter confirmed that no re-grout outside the `~regrout` argument runs during a parse. It counted 0 on all 72 programs, and a build deliberately passing `~regrout=true` counted 351 on one small file.
- **Parse-related test groups** (`TextRoundtrip.*`, `DocSlides`, `ImpliedHole`, the round-trip groups, `ShardCrashRepro`): all 386 tests pass on both `dev` and this branch.
- **Full suite:** all 4522 tests pass (283 s locally).

## Timings

Parse time for the 72 `hazel-programs`, one run per row unless noted. Single runs of the same build differ by up to about 4%.

| Build | Total | vs `dev` |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` | 217–222 s (3 runs) | |
| + (1) | 218 s | within noise |
| + (2) | 176 s | −19% |
| + (3) | 166 s | −24% |
| + (4) | 87 s | **−61%** |

On its own, (1) saved 39.2 s against 44.6 s on the three slowest files (mean of 3 alternating runs). The full-corpus runs can't tell it apart from noise.

The parse-related test groups take **142 s instead of 267 s**.

## Added after review of coverage

Codecov flagged 6 changed lines as never run. Two more commits:

5. **Code no test could reach is gone.** The `~regrout` defaults on three functions that every caller passes explicitly are now required. The unused `Segment.rescan` is removed. So is `rescan_reassemble`'s `|| siblings == …` fallback, since after (1) and (3) identity is exact. A new group, `Parser.LoadPath`, pins the contract that identity now rests on: `Siblings.rescan` returns the very same pair when nothing changes.
6. **Text with Windows line endings loads without a hole on every line.** `"\r\n"` is one grapheme, so the parsers never saw the lone `"\r"` they skipped, and every line after the first loaded with a `¿` hole at its start. `dev` does the same today; this was the uncovered line. It's fixed in `to_zipper` (load and paste) and in `to_segment`. Two tests check it, and both fail without the fix.

A second coverage pass found 4 more uncovered lines, all in the line-ending code. A lone `"\r"` was being skipped, which glued the tokens on either side of it: `let x = 1 in\rx` loaded as `…inx`. It now reads as `"\n"`, like `"\r\n"`. The fourth line, a failed insertion ending the parse, now has a test.

Full suite after all of these: 4528 pass.

## The large livelit slides

The corpus's largest program is about 7 KB, so it missed the single-expression livelit slides, 10–23 KB with no safe split points. Timing those found a memory bug in (2): `to_zipper`'s new loop recursed through `let*`, which js_of_ocaml doesn't turn into a loop. That left a stack frame per run of characters, each holding the zipper it started from. Kids' Choice and Tree Care overflowed the stack, or ran out of a 4 GB heap, where `dev` parses them.

7. **A direct self call fixes it.** js_of_ocaml compiles that to a loop, as the old `fold_left` was.

`MarkerParse.of_text` in node, heap capped at 500 MB, one run each, `dev` against this branch, structure identical on all four:

| Slide | Size | `dev` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tuples | 5.6 KB | 8.9 s | 2.0 s |
| 1990s Face | 10 KB | 67.6 s | 25.8 s |
| Emotion (Kids' Choice) | 22 KB | 302.7 s | 119.4 s |
| Tree Care | 23 KB | 441.4 s | 168.7 s |

No test in the suite catches the leak. It needs thousands of runs, and at the sizes where it shows, the parse is too slow for a test. Full suite after the fix: 4526 pass.

## Not in this PR

- Paste could use `~by_run` too, but that path has more cases (a live zipper, selections, neighbours on both sides), so it deserves its own check.
- Each re-grout still walks the whole run. Making it local to the edit would also speed up ordinary typing in long expressions, but that's a change to the editor core.

commits.messageBody:
Siblings.rescan rebuilt its pair with @ and split_n even when neither
side held an incomplete tile, so rescan_reassemble's structural ==
walked every sibling on every insertion. Return the argument itself in
that case and check === first.

Same printed output on all 72 hazel-programs; on the three slowest,
39.2 s vs 44.6 s (mean of 3 alternating runs), though single
full-corpus runs show the gap within noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Let rescan say "no change" by identity, so typing skips a deep compare

commits.messageBody:
Parser.to_zipper gains ~by_run: when the caret is between tokens, the
longest run that stays one operand (or one operator) goes in as a
single Insert.go, which is what typing it would append to anyway.
Brackets, quotes, comment delimiters and whitespace still come one at
a time. Only MarkerParse.of_text passes it; paste is unchanged.

Same printed output on all 72 hazel-programs; total parse time 217 s
to 176 s (one run each).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Load text a token at a time, not a character at a time

commits.messageBody:
Mid-parse there is nearly always an open tile (a let awaiting its in),
so the early return in Siblings.rescan rarely fired and
rescan_reassemble still compared every sibling structurally.
Segment.rescan_changed now says whether any piece came out different
(comparing the one converted piece, since a conversion can return an
equal one), and Siblings.rescan hands back its argument when nothing
was presplit or converted.

Same printed output on all 72 hazel-programs; total parse time 176 s
to 166 s (one run each).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Let rescan report "no change" even while a tile is incomplete

commits.messageBody:
Regrouting walks the whole sibling run, so doing it after each
insertion made MarkerParse.of_text quadratic in the length of a run.
Insert.go (and the helpers it uses, plus Zipper.put_down_target) take
~regrout=true; Parser.to_zipper ~by_run passes false and regrouts once
at the end. Every other caller keeps the default, so typing, paste and
destruction are unchanged.

Checked against dev on all 72 hazel-programs: identical structure
(labels, molds, shards, grout shapes, whitespace; ids aside). The
parse-related groups (TextRoundtrip, DocSlides, ImpliedHole,
round-trip, ShardCrashRepro) pass, 386 tests, in 142 s vs 267 s.
Total parse time on the 72 programs: 166 s to 87 s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Regrout once when loading text, not after every insertion

commits.messageBody:
…ach goes

Codecov flagged 6 changed lines. Four were unreachable:
- the `~regrout: bool=true` defaults on insert_shard, split and
  insert_or_append, which every caller passes explicitly; now required;
- Segment.rescan, which nothing calls since Siblings takes
  rescan_changed; removed;
- rescan_reassemble's `|| siblings == ...` fallback. Siblings.rescan
  hands back its argument exactly when nothing changed, so the
  structural comparison could never be the one to say "unchanged";
  identity is the whole test now.

New group Parser.LoadPath pins that contract: rescan returns the very
same pair with no incomplete tile, and with a one-shard incomplete tile
that has nothing to match (a multi-shard orphan is presplit, which is
a change by design).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Rescan's "no change" is identity alone, and the code no test could re…

commits.messageBody:
Token.to_list segments by grapheme, and "\r\n" is ONE grapheme, so
text saved with CRLF endings reached Parser.to_zipper as "\r\n"
characters, never as the lone "\r" it skipped. Each was inserted as an
unknown token, leaving a `¿` hole at the start of every following line:
`let x = 1 in\r\nlet y ...` loaded as `let x = 1 in\n¿let y ...`. Same
on dev before this PR; the `\r` branch was the line Codecov found
uncovered.

line_ending reads "\r\n" as "\n" and still skips a lone "\r", in
to_zipper (load and paste) and in to_segment (#2610's load path), whose
split check now also sees the normalized newline.

Parser.LoadPath: `\r\n` loads like `\n`, and segments like it; both
fail without this change. Full suite: 4526 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: Text with Windows line endings loads without a hole on every line

commits.messageBody:
`let* z = insert(z, s); go(z, rest)` recursed through Option.bind's
closure, which js_of_ocaml does not turn into a loop: a stack frame per
run of characters, each holding the zipper it started from. The result
was right, but on the 20 KB livelit slides the parse overflowed the
stack, or with a larger stack ran out of a 4 GB heap: Emotion (Kids'
Choice) and Tree Care both failed where dev parses them. A 9 KB prefix
needed over 800 MB of heap on this branch and under 500 MB on dev. The
old fold_left kept only the current zipper; a direct self call now does
the same, and js_of_ocaml compiles it to a loop.

Measured with MarkerParse.of_text in node, heap capped at 500 MB, one
run each, dev vs this branch, structure identical on all four:
Tuples 8.9 s -> 2.0 s; 1990s Face 67.6 s -> 25.8 s; Kids' Choice
302.7 s -> 119.4 s; Tree Care 441.4 s -> 168.7 s. No test in the suite
catches this: the leak needs thousands of runs, which parse too slowly
for a test at the sizes where it shows. Full suite: 4526 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: to_zipper's loop no longer keeps every intermediate zipper alive

commits.messageBody:
Codecov's last 4 uncovered lines were all here. Three were the lone
"\r" case: line_ending skipped it, and both parsers acted on that
skip. But skipping glues the tokens either side, so `let x = 1 in\rx`
loaded as `... inx`. A lone "\r" (old Mac endings, or a stray one) now
reads as "\n", like "\r\n"; line_ending always answers a character, and
the two skip branches are gone.

The fourth was to_zipper's `None => None`: an insertion that fails ends
the parse. Now tested by starting from a zipper whose caret is inside a
token with nothing after it, where Insert.go has nothing to insert
into.

Parser.LoadPath: a lone \r loads like \n (fails with the old skip), and
a failed insertion ends the parse with None. Full suite: 4528 pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
commits.messageHeadline: A lone carriage return is a line break, not nothing

title: Load text about 2.5× faster: whole tokens, one re-grout
